referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with brand/logo presence, large headline, short supporting copy, and a compact bullet-value list; CTA emphasis is primarily via a prominent trial/demo action rather than multiple competing buttons.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top hero band followed by vertically stacked content sections; each section uses a strong headline, brief explanatory paragraph, then a feature grid/list. Rhythm is content-led with clear separation between modules rather than dense mixed layouts.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily simple informational cards/feature blocks with minimal ornamentation; content appears in clean white/light panels, basic icon-accented bullets, and restrained borders/shadows if any.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Single primary conversion CTA in hero/form area; supporting sections are mostly informational and do not introduce repeated CTA clutter. Lead capture is prioritized through an adjacent form module.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern evident in the provided reference excerpt.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference excerpt; no footer pattern can be reliably extracted.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible reference: logo mark, small inline tick icons, and no heavy imagery. Visual communication relies on typography and icon bullets rather than large product visuals.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential product-benefit sections with repeated headline + description + feature-list structure. Sections read as modular blocks that can be scanned quickly, likely using multi-column feature rows on desktop and stacked cards on mobile.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed near the hero; compact title, hidden tracking fields, and a structured input area. Form is treated as a high-priority conversion module with clear containment and separation from informational content.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit motion system is visible in the excerpt; interaction style appears static and utility-driven rather than animation-heavy.
componentPatterns: benefit bullet list with tick icons
designNotes: Design language is functional and enterprise-oriented.
Hierarchy is driven by large headings, concise subcopy, and listable benefits.
Conversion is supported by an immediately visible form rather than long progressive persuasion.
The layout favors clarity and rapid scanning over visual complexity.
Reusable pattern should prioritize modular sections, strong typography, and compact trust/benefit messaging.

personality.buyer: Administrators, IT teams, MSSPs, and compliance-focused organizations
personality.emotion: controlled urgency, operational confidence, and audit-grade trust
personality.reasoning: Firewall Analyzer is a security operations product built for visibility, monitoring, compliance, and incident investigation. The visual language should feel precise, technical, and dependable rather than flashy. Use a dark-forward, command-center style with strong contrast, structured grids, and intelligent data panels. Brand orange from techjockey.com should be used as the primary energy point for CTA and hero emphasis, while the rest of the palette stays restrained to support trust and clarity.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and technically dense, so 48px keeps it authoritative without breaking the split hero layout.

colours.colourReason: Primary is grounded in the brand's dark neutral for a premium security feel, while accent uses the exact brand orange for CTA and key highlights. The palette avoids generic blue/purple security tropes and stays fully derived from brand colors.

backgroundSystem.hero: Solid #1a1a1a with subtle orange edge glow and faint grid overlay

layout.heroBackground: Dark charcoal hero with a layered command-center visual on the right
layout.heroReason: The product benefits from a split hero because firewall analytics are easiest to communicate with an interface-led visual. The left side carries clear value proposition and CTA, while the right side uses a PNG dashboard mockup, floating metric chips, and log-stream panels to signal operational intelligence.
layout.featureReason: Five operational features are best presented as a strong spotlight row followed by a structured grid. This lets the platform capabilities feel both premium and practical, while maintaining strong readability for IT buyers.
layout.darkSectionFor: hero, mid-page proof band, and final CTA strip to create contrast and a command-center rhythm

personality.imageryDirection: Use a high-clarity product interface visual with layered monitoring panels, log tables, anomaly alerts, bandwidth charts, and compliance report cards. Keep it realistic and enterprise-grade, with subtle orange highlights on active states. Add floating chips like 'Real-time monitoring', 'Compliance ready', and 'Log forensics' to create depth. If product imagery is limited, build a CSS-based dashboard shell with chart blocks, table rows, and status pills.
personality.designPersonality: A precise, command-center security aesthetic: dark, disciplined, and trustworthy, with orange as the only high-energy accent. The page should feel like a premium network operations cockpit — layered panels, clear hierarchy, strong borders, intelligent data visualization, and minimal decorative noise.

componentNeeds.variantHint: security product hero with prominent CTA and compact value bullets
componentNeeds.notes: Use strong authority styling, concise supporting copy, and one dominant action. Keep the hero visually disciplined and technical, not promotional. Since no image is provided, favor a text-led hero with bullet-value list and high contrast.

componentNeeds.variantHint: 3-column grid on desktop, stacked on mobile
componentNeeds.notes: Present firewall compatibility and key capabilities as a modular feature section. Make the first row about supported firewalls, then scan-friendly benefit cards. Prioritize agentless analytics, monitoring, bandwidth analysis, log investigation, and policy management.

componentNeeds.variantHint: 3-column or 2x2 card layout depending on available width
componentNeeds.notes: Frame these as business outcomes for IT teams: configuration change tracking, compliance audits, centralized reporting, and security oversight. Keep text dense enough to inform but not overwhelm.
Surface low TCO, faster productivity, actionable insights, quick deployment, and broader device visibility. Use this section to support decision-makers who need operational justification.
Use the two available testimonials only. Emphasize role and industry context to make the proof feel relevant to IT managers and heads of IT.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a strong dark or deep authority-colored hero background with white text, a short supporting line, and a single prominent primary CTA. Because there is no product screenshot, keep the hero centered or slightly split with a compact bullet-value list rather than a visual-heavy layout. Avoid secondary CTA clutter.
layoutStrategy.features: Stack vertically with clear module separation. Each section should begin with a bold headline and short description, followed by a clean feature grid. Use 3-column cards on desktop for the 5-item and 4-item sections, then collapse to single-column on mobile.
layoutStrategy.proof: Introduce testimonials after the value sections so proof arrives once the product story is established. Keep the cards clean, with clear author hierarchy and a restrained layout to maintain trust.
layoutStrategy.pricing: No pricing section should be introduced because no pricing content is available in the source input.
layoutStrategy.form: No form module should be added because includeForm is false in the context. Conversion should rely on the hero CTA and overall page persuasion rather than lead-capture form placement.

designIntent.figmaReadySummary: Design a single-product, lead-generation landing page for a firewall security tool.
